clue.text: Finally wheel in lots of compost

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: lots means much, a great deal

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word wheel

explanation.surface: A gardener finally barrows in a great load of compost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes L, the last letter of 'wheel', and 'in' puts it inside MUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of compost or rotted matter spread on soil is called by this gardening term.

clue.text: Devious smile is weapon

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the letters of smile is take a twisted order

explanation.surface: A crafty grin is a weapon of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' shuffles SMILE and IS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket or projectile is a kind of weapon that is fired or thrown.

clue.text: Eccentric minority's bizarre fencing ritual

indicators.note: bizarre means weird, so the letters of fencing ritual come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A cult of oddballs holds a strange swordplay ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' shuffles FENCING RITUAL; the 's is read as 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the extreme, odd fringe members of a group or movement.

clue.text: Greeting hill girl with no guarantee of result

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a miss is a young girl or unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a girl on a hilltop may or may not work out.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a craggy hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something random or haphazard, whose outcome cannot be relied on.

clue.text: Improve cutting edge of small instrument in from France

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a harp is a stringed musical instrument
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: Someone improves a small instrument brought in from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Honing a blade or knife improves its cutting edge, which is the verb wanted.

clue.text: Flower section found in forest amenity

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words forest amenity

explanation.surface: A flower part turns up among the facilities of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' hides the answer in foreST AMENity.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing male organ is one part of a blossom, so a flower section.

clue.text: By the sound of it, everyone's hand tool

indicators.note: by the sound of it tells us to say a word aloud and spell what we hear differently

parts.note: everyone is all, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: Apparently, this is a hand tool belonging to everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the sound of it' turns ALL into its spoken twin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed spike for piercing leather or wood is a simple hand tool.

clue.text: Spectator upset with rain delay

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so the letters of spectator with rain are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unhappy onlooker watches the rain hold up play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles SPECTATOR and RAIN as one pool; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off doing something is to stall or defer it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Ultimately drawn to the traditional Christmas

indicators.note: ultimately takes the closing letter of each of the four words drawn to the traditional

explanation.surface: In the end people are drawn to a traditional Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes the last letters of 'drawn', 'to', 'the', 'traditional'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-derived word for the festive season appears in carols and on cards.

clue.text: Fans in a train embracing singer

indicators.note: embracing says the words fans in a train hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Fans on a train cluster around a celebrity vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' hides the answer in fanS IN A TRAin; 'Fans' looks like admirers but just supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank of that surname was a famous American crooner, so a singer.

clue.text: John's English, imprecise

parts.note: john is US slang for a toilet, as is loo, so johns are loos

explanation.surface: Someone called John speaks vague English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name but is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Vague, inexact wording or a rough translation is described as being free or slack.

clue.text: Go-between, tidy earner, I'm excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of tidy earner and I'm are mixed together

explanation.surface: A middleman thrilled at earning a tidy sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' shuffles TIDY EARNER and IM as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator or broker acting between two parties is a synonym of go-between.

clue.text: Private hotel on lively Rome street

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: lively means animated, so the letters of Rome are stirred about

explanation.surface: A private hotel stands on a bustling street in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively' rearranges ROME into ERMO; 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts that are most personal and hidden are private ones.

clue.text: You heard about top Greek mathematician

indicators.note: heard tells us the word you is spoken aloud and spelt in another way

parts.note: the word you said aloud, written another way
C stands for circa, Latin for about
a lid is a top or cover

explanation.surface: You've heard something about a top Greek mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns YOU into EU, a spelling that is said the same way; C is circa, about.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of the Elements, founder of geometry, was an ancient Greek of Alexandria.

clue.text: Boy following college agreement

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the boy goes after the college

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy following his college choice reaches a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the boy first, but 'following' means he comes second in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in total accord, all speaking at once, is concord or agreement.

clue.text: Run over on regular basis, see army's place for young

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word run is written backwards
on a regular basis means taking every other letter of see army's

explanation.surface: Regularly running over to see the army's childcare facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses RUN to NUR; 'on regular basis' takes SERY, alternate letters of 'see army's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or school where small children are looked after is a place for the young.

clue.text: Spat, extremely prevalent conflict

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters, of the word spat

parts.note: rife means widespread or prevalent

explanation.surface: A quarrel shows the widespread conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes ST, the outer letters of 'Spat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter disagreement or discord is a synonym of conflict.

clue.text: Rishi trained reservist's dog

indicators.note: trained means schooled or reshaped, so the letters of Rishi are reworked

parts.note: a terrier is slang for a member of the Territorial Army, a British reservist

explanation.surface: Rishi trained the dog belonging to a part-time soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges RISHI; TERRIER is slang for a British Territorial Army volunteer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of terrier from Ireland with a wiry red coat, so a dog.

clue.text: Short distance seeing favourites upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as with a teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A slight gap appears with favourites in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses PETS; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One pace or stride covers only a little way, so a short distance.

clue.text: Trade union recalled offence, capital

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: A trade union remembered an offence committed in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses SIN to NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the North African coast is the capital of Tunisia.

clue.text: When speaking, catch sight of the drink

indicators.note: when speaking says a word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: to catch sight of something is to see it

explanation.surface: Someone says out loud that they spot a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When speaking' turns SEE into its sound-alike. 'The drink' is slang for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is informal slang for the ocean, as in falling into the drink.

clue.text: Island very behind time cut off

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
late means behind time

explanation.surface: An island, very much behind the times, is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or quarantine something is to set it apart, a synonym of cut off.

clue.text: Look to mature nobles

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A command to look to the older members of the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective body of lords and titled aristocrats in Britain is the nobility.

clue.text: Very small golfers' support provided by New York

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A golfers' prop comes from New York in a tiny size.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word for tiny or minute describes something very small.
